title: TimeSkeleton manifest
description: The TimeSkeleton 0.7.0 manifest, an exchange format for the structures of musical timelines without their events: their axes, extents, nesting, groups, conversion maps, regions, flow control and measure maps. Music-research software trades these structures in it like a currency. The format expresses the TimeToAlign! model (TISMIR, https://doi.org/10.5334/tismir.296); the Python library timetoalign is one implementation of it. Every manifest is one AlignmentBundle with an array of one or multiple root timelines, optionally named, optionally attributing timelines to groups, optionally styled for drawing (`docs/drawing.md`). Time coordinates use the model's time units and number-type primitives: a fraction is a [numerator, denominator] pair of integers with a strictly positive denominator, an integer is a JSON integer and a float is a JSON number. Every object is open: the schema closes none, and a key an object does not declare is kept and reported as unknown by the TimeSkeleton validators, never refused. Every key with a default may be left out; a reader supplies the default. The definitions TimeSkeleton, Timeline, Group, Graphical, ConversionMap, Coordinate, Number, Fraction, TimeUnit, NumberType, Id and MeasureMapRow are public: a host may refer to this document or to `#/$defs/<name>`, and they change only by addition within 0.7.x.

TimeSkeleton.description: A TimeSkeleton manifest: one or more root timelines with all their descendants (child timelines), optionally named, optionally attributing timelines to groups, and optionally styled. A single timeline is represented as a manifest of a single root; a TimelineGroup is represented as a manifest with a single group. A manifest with an ID or a name constitutes a named AlignmentBundle, one with neither is anonymous. Timeline IDs (of roots and descendants), group IDs and the manifest ID are unique together; every other ID (of a conversion map, region, break, jump or marker) is unique within its root's tree. A timeline, a group or the manifest is addressed by its bare ID and every other element by `<root ID>/<element ID>`; an element's parts follow its address as `/start`, `/end`, `/name`, `/label` and `/card`, so none of these five words may be an ID. The manifest's title is addressed `name`. Object keys carry no order and are written sorted by code point. The roots and the groups are written sorted by ID and each group's members by code point; readers accept any order.

$schema.description: The URL of this schema, a hint for editors. It is never read.

timeskeleton.description: The TimeSkeleton version this manifest conforms to. Compulsory: a JSON structure without it is not a TimeSkeleton manifest.

name.description: The manifest's human-readable name, its title, or null when none was given.

timelines.description: The root timelines, each with all its descendants. The array may be empty.

groups.description: The timeline groups. A root that no group names remains ungrouped in the bundle. A root whose descendants are named in a group is indirectly linked with that group.

Timeline.description: One timeline without its events: its axis (unit and number type), its length, its children, conversion maps, regions, flow control, measure map and metric hierarchy. The unit decides the timeline's domain and modality. Every coordinate on the timeline's own axis (its length, its children's offsets, region bounds, break and marker coordinates, jump coordinates) is a bare Number represented as the axis's number type selects: a JSON integer for int, a JSON number for float, a Fraction pair for fraction. Arrays have one canonical order: children by offset, then ID; conversion maps by ID; regions by start, end, ID; breaks and markers by coordinate, then ID; jumps by from and to coordinate, then ID. Readers accept any order.

number_type.description: The number type of every coordinate on the timeline's axis. Absent means the unit's default number type, which the unit table (`TimeUnit`) states for every unit.

length.description: The end of the timeline on its own axis, or null when the length is not known.

offset.description: Where the timeline's origin lies. A child's offset is required, lies on its parent's axis, in the parent's number type, and may be negative: the child then starts before its parent's origin. A root's offset is optional, may be negative, and places the root's origin on its unit's absolute axis; typically absent.

locked.description: Whether the timeline's extent is fixed. A locked timeline, such as a CD track, cannot extend; an unlocked one may grow, as a CD timeline built by appending track after track does.

is_segment_line.description: Whether the timeline is a segment line: a timeline containing only contiguous segments. Its children are its segments: each shares the segment line's unit, as every child shares its parent's; they are contiguous from 0 in offset order (a segment of unknown length ends where its successor starts) and end at its length where both are known, all with one is_segment_line value; segments that are segment lines themselves make a nested segment line. Contiguity and the one is_segment_line value are checked after the schema.

children.description: The child timelines, each carrying its offset on this timeline's axis.

conversion_maps.description: Conversion maps attached to this timeline.

measure_map.description: The measure map, or null. A measure map is anchored in note values, so only a timeline whose unit is quarters or whole_note may carry one.

metric_hierarchy.description: The metric hierarchy, or null; an object without further constraints.

Timeline.$comment: Only a timeline in quarters or whole_note, the symbolic note-value units, may hold a measure map. Any other unit leaves measure_map out or null.

Group.description: A timeline group: member timelines sharing, by definition, the same graphical start and end. Every member's 0 coincides with every other member's 0 and every member's length with every other member's length, and positions in between convert linearly; a member's length may be unknown. It is possible for child timelines to participate in a group. A group is defined by naming member timelines of the manifest, roots or children at any depth; a timeline may be a member of several groups, and no member lies inside or contains another member of the same group. A child may belong to a group while its root belongs to another or to none.

members.description: The IDs of the member timelines, sorted by code point. The array may be empty.

Graphical.description: How the manifest is drawn (`docs/drawing.md`): named styles, an ordered list of statements, the display order of each group's members and the band order of each timeline. A statement selects drawn elements and sets presentation properties on them, either directly or by naming a style of `styles`; a name that `styles` does not hold sets nothing. Writers never reorder the statements or an order. An absent block draws every element with the other style layers alone.

statements.description: Statements in order; of two statements of equal rank the later one decides.

order.description: The order of what a group or a timeline stacks, top to bottom, keyed by a group's ID (the display order of its members) or by a timeline's ID, of a root or a descendant (its band order). A group without an entry is displayed in the order of its members; a timeline without one follows its parent's band order, band by band ID, and a root without one the default band order.

ConversionMap.description: A conversion map of a timeline, discriminated by its type.

Coordinate.description: A self-describing position: the axis unit, the number type, and the value in the representation that number type selects. Inside a manifest every position lies on an axis its container declares (a timeline's unit and number type, a conversion map's source and target units) and is a bare Number; this form is for a position outside such a container, as hosts exchange single positions.

value.description: The position, represented as selected by number_type.

oneOf.description: An integer coordinate.
A float coordinate.
An exact fraction coordinate.

Number.description: A bare JSON number or an exact Fraction pair.

Fraction.description: Rational number encoded as a numerator and a non-zero denominator, each written as a JSON integer. JSON Schema also considers a number with a zero fractional part to be an integer; the TimeSkeleton validators refuse such a member when it was written as a float.

prefixItems.description: Denominator. Strictly positive to prevent zero-division and negative bases.

TimeUnit.description: The unit of a timeline axis. Each unit belongs to one domain (logical: musical time; physical: real time; graphical: space) and one modality (continuous or discrete), and states the default number type of an axis that declares none. The domain and modality decide the timeline class: `seconds`, physical and continuous, makes a ContinuousPhysicalTimeline.

oneOf.description: Logical, continuous; default number type float.
Logical, continuous; default number type float.
Logical, continuous; default number type fraction.
Logical, continuous; default number type fraction.
Logical, discrete; default number type int.
Physical, continuous; default number type float.
Physical, continuous; default number type float.
Physical, continuous; default number type float.
Physical, discrete; default number type int.
Physical, discrete; default number type int.
Graphical, discrete; default number type int.

NumberType.description: The number type of every coordinate on a timeline axis. It selects the representation of a coordinate's value: int is a JSON integer, float a JSON number, fraction a Fraction pair.

Id.description: An identifier: a non-empty string without '/' and without control characters (U+0000 to U+001F); spaces are allowed. An ID identifies; a name, where an element has one, is what is displayed.

Address.description: An element address as the drawing specification (`docs/drawing.md`) defines it: an ID, followed by zero or more parts, each a `/` and a non-empty string without `/` and without control characters.

Name.description: Human-readable name, or null when none was given.

MeasureMapRow.description: One row of the Measure Map standard plus the TimeSkeleton extensions volta and offset_within_measure.

ID.description: Any unique string to identify this Measure object. Unique, here, means that the string cannot be used as ID for another object that forms part of the same MeasureMap. The 'next' array may use these IDs to refer to other Measures. Additionally, IDs can prove useful in cross-relating between MeasureMaps relating to different editions of the same piece, e.g. by assigning identical IDs for measures that are identical across the two. The ID could be, for instance, human-readable form (e.g., the 'count' value converted to a string) or a random string (often the case in MEI scores).

count.description: Position of this Measure object in the MeasureMap, using natural numbers starting with 1. This serves primarily as an index, and does not attempt detailed musical conventions. In the simplest case (e.g., a score with no anacrusis or other irregularities) this count matches the (most musical) number field below.

qstamp.description: The symbolic time to have elapsed since the beginning of the source, measured in quarter notes. Non-negative; TimeSkeleton additionally permits an exact Fraction pair.

number.description: A number assigned to this measure based on a given set of rules or conventions. One wide-spread convention, for instance, is that a piece starts with measure number 0 if it has an anacrusis and with number 1 otherwise.

name.description: A label for the Measure. Typically used for distinguishing between Measures with the same number, e.g. for first and second endings (as in '16a', '16b') or split logical measures (as in '16-1', '16-2').

time_signature.description: A label for the time signature. Typically this takes the form <int>/<int>, as in ‘3/8’, but can be any text (e.g., ‘C’, ‘common time’, ‘unmeasured’ ‘cadenza’) as long as actual_length is specified.

nominal_length.description: The default duration that corresponds to the given 'time_signature', in quarter notes. Can be derived from 'time_signature' if it takes the form of an '<int>/<int>'-encoded fraction. Can take the value 'null' if the time signature has no corresponding duration (e.g. 'cadenza'). TimeSkeleton additionally permits an exact Fraction pair.

actual_length.description: The actual duration of the measure, in quarter notes. Strictly positive; TimeSkeleton additionally permits an exact Fraction pair.

start_repeat.description: Typical usage is with the bool type, with 'true' indicating a start repeat at the beginning of the measure.

end_repeat.description: Typical usage is with the bool type, with 'true' indicating an end repeat at the end of the measure.

next.description: The 'ID' strings or 'count' integers that correspond to all measures that can follow this one. The corresponding field needs to be present in the MeasureMap.

volta.description: A TimeSkeleton extension that identifies the volta ending. It carries no structural constraint.

offset_within_measure.description: A TimeSkeleton extension: where this row begins inside its nominal measure, in quarter notes, when the row represents only part of that measure (an anacrusis, or one constituent of a split measure). Absent means 0; a row never states 0.

NumberNonnegative.description: A non-negative bare JSON number or a non-negative exact Fraction pair.

NumberPositive.description: A strictly positive bare JSON number or a strictly positive exact Fraction pair.

FractionNonnegative.description: A Fraction whose numerator is non-negative.

FractionPositive.description: A Fraction whose numerator is strictly positive.

Region.description: A region of a timeline, from start to end on the timeline's own axis.

FlowControl.description: The flow control of a timeline: its breaks, jumps and flow markers. A flow marker is a named position that jumps target; the markers band does not draw it. It differs from a coordinate marker, a wedge the markers band draws at a root's start and end.

Break.description: A flow-control break at a coordinate on the timeline's own axis.

Jump.description: A flow-control jump from one coordinate to another on the timeline's own axis.

target.description: The ID of the marker of the same timeline this jump targets, or null.

Marker.description: A flow marker: a named position on the timeline's own axis, the target of jumps. Flow control holds it and nothing draws it; the markers band holds the coordinate markers instead, the wedges at a root's start and end.

MeasureMap.description: Compressed rows from the Measure Map standard. A row equal to its predecessor's default successor is omitted as a whole.

Order.description: One order of `graphical.order`, top to bottom, never reordered by a writer: a group's display order, a permutation of its members' IDs, or a timeline's band order, a permutation of the timeline's ID `T` and its five band addresses `T/markers_1`, `T/conversion_maps_1`, `T/children_1`, `T/regions_1` and `T/flow_control_1`. The markers band holds the coordinate markers, the wedges at a root's start and end, never the flow markers of `flow_control`. Each entry is an ID, or an ID, `/` and a band's ID: its kind, `_` and its number.

Statement.description: One statement: the elements it selects and the properties it sets on them, as a declaration or as the name of a style.

oneOf.description: The name of a style of the same block's `styles`.

Selector.description: An element matches when it matches every member present. The empty selector matches every element.

ids.description: Element addresses; the element's address must be one of them.

domain.description: The domain of the element: what its time measures (graphical space, musical time, physical time).

modality.description: Whether the element is continuous or discrete.

class.description: The class of the element: the timeline class its unit decides, a conversion map's type, or a band's kind.

within.description: A timeline ID: the element must belong to that timeline or to one of its descendants.

inside.description: An element type: the element must be held, at any depth, by an element of that type in the drawing's element tree.

ElementType.description: The type of an element of the drawing: the box's background, a root timeline's line (a group member's or an ungrouped root's), a child timeline's line at any depth, one of the five bands of a timeline (which draws nothing of its own and holds the timeline's coordinate markers, conversion maps, children, regions or flow control), a conversion map, a region, a flow-control break or jump, a wedge (a coordinate marker at a root's start or end; the flow markers of `flow_control` are not drawn), a name in the name column (or the title of a group or of the manifest), any other text label, a segment's boundary tick on its segment line, an ancestor line of a member that is a child timeline, a group's frame, or the raised card holding a timeline drawn in its own card.

Paint.description: A colour as #RRGGBB with upper-case hexadecimal digits, or none.

Declaration.description: Presentation properties. Where SVG has the property, it carries SVG's name; content, max-width and shadow are TimeSkeleton's own, SVG having no property of that meaning. An element reads only the properties its type reads; the others are ignored.

stroke-dasharray.description: none, or non-negative decimal numbers separated by single spaces.

MapBase.description: What every conversion map carries: its type, its ID, its name, and the units of the axes it converts from and to, either null where that side is not a time axis. Each map type adds its own members.

type.description: The map type, which each map definition fixes.

source_unit.description: The unit of the axis the map converts from, or null.

target_unit.description: The unit of the axis the map converts to, or null.

MetricalPositionMap.description: Metrical position (measure count and beat) of a quarter position. Its two outputs are derived from meter_map: the measure count by the meter map itself, the beat by a BeatInMeasureMap whose ID is beat_map_id.

beat_map_id.description: The ID of the BeatInMeasureMap derived from meter_map.
